title: MutableDataFrame must accept writes to its derived length during object copying
answers: Why does Explore’s raw Prometheus view crash with multiple instant queries?
Why does cloneDeep(props.data) throw in a plugin under an ESM build?
Why does MutableDataFrame have an empty length setter?
Can RawListContainer use the supplied tableResult directly?
body:
Symptom: Explore’s raw Prometheus view with two or more instant queries, or a plugin cloning its data, can throw “Cannot set property length … which has only a getter” under strict ESM builds.
Root cause: packages/grafana-data/src/dataframe/MutableDataFrame.ts:MutableDataFrame.length was getter-only; generic copiers recreate the prototype and assign properties, including length. public/app/features/explore/PrometheusListView/RawListContainer.tsx:RawListContainer unnecessarily deep-cloned the merged frame.
Fix pattern: Keep a no-op setter for the derived length so generic copiers can assign it without throwing; read-only consumers such as RawListContainer can use the supplied frame directly.
Constraints: Length remains derived from the first field, so assigning it must not resize the frame or override the getter’s value. Direct frame reuse applies to consumers that only read it; consumers that mutate data need a separate ownership decision.
applies: Changes to MutableDataFrame’s length accessor, generic frame copying, or Explore’s read-only raw Prometheus list.
